text: A coin lands heads 99.9% of the time. Its entropy is 0.0114 bits per flip. What follows?
choices: The coin is broken, since a fair source is required for entropy to be defined.
A thousand such flips carry about 11 bits in total and could be transmitted in two bytes.
The entropy will rise toward 1 as more flips are observed and the estimate improves.
Each flip must still be stored in one bit, since a bit is the smallest addressable unit.
explanation: Predictable data is cheap to transmit and unpredictable data is not — that curve is the whole practical content of the chapter. The source coding theorem makes it exact: a source of entropy H can be encoded in H bits per symbol on average, and no encoding does better. So H is not an estimate; it is the size of the data.
